title: The 56 agencies drawn: all 28 usable agencies serving 500,000 or more, and 28 sampled from 8 region-by-size strata
subtitle: 54 enter the comparison; 2 have too few years before 1995. Fill gives each agency's change in deaths per resident (exact Poisson test, p < .05). Markers sit at the LEAIC's point for each agency, so a city and its county overlap.

title: Pooled, fatal police shootings are about where they were before 1995 (0.97); the typical agency kills about twice as many people a year (2.01)
subtitle: 52 agencies, design-weighted, with 95% CIs (t on 45 df). The pooled ratio weights agencies by their deaths, so large departments dominate it; the typical-agency ratio is the mean of each agency's own log ratio.

title: 7 of the 10 largest departments have lower rates per resident than before 1995; 25 of the other 42 have higher rates (point estimates)
subtitle: One point per agency, sized by population served. Departments with high rates before 1995 mostly fell and those with low rates mostly rose. Axes are log-like above 0.05 and linear near zero, so agencies with no deaths in an era sit on the axis.

title: Per resident, 12 of the 52 agencies kill clearly fewer people than before 1995, 11 clearly more
subtitle: Grey dot: before 1995; colored dot: 2015–25. In the other 29, the change is too small to tell from chance (exact Poisson test, p < .05). Population is the SHR median for 1985–94 and 2015–24 (LEAIC 2012 where the SHR has none).

title: In the same agencies, the SHR records 94% of the deaths counted here before 1995, but only 56% since 2015
subtitle: Top: deaths a year in the 52 sample agencies (design-weighted Poisson model with agency fixed effects, 95% CI), about 122 in 2015–25 against 100 in 1985–94. The early 1970s, with only a few large cities, ran far higher, so the pre-registered pooled ratio over 1970–94 is 0.97 (0.69–1.35). Middle: the SHR's share of these deaths, where the agency filed.
note: Counts are hand-built, or WaPo/MPV where 07 splices them in. The SHR share uses agency-years where the agency filed (Florida agencies file none) and ends in 2024; the drop after 2020 coincides with the FBI's move to NIBRS. The LA County Sheriff's 1985–90 period total has no yearly breakdown and is left out of this figure.

title: The typical-agency ratio stays well above 1 in every run; the pooled ratio depends on a few large departments and on the early 1970s
subtitle: The pooled ratio rises without the four largest departments, and when the early era starts in 1985, since a few large cities ran far higher in the 1970s. Runs below the dashed rule were added after the results and were not pre-registered. Zero-handling runs apply to the typical-agency ratio only. Every run is in sample_estimates.csv.
